ERA V5 Session 8 · Position

RoPE makes distance visible to attention

The query–key dot product compares content, but it does not say how far apart two tokens are. RoPE adds that missing clue by rotating query and key vectors according to their positions.

RoPE is on. The score can now respond to distance. Moving both tokens together changes positions 2 and 8, but their gap stays 6—so the score stays 0.500.
The two tokens in the sequence

Without position

For this demonstration, query and key begin as identical content vectors. Their dot product cannot reveal the gap.

With RoPE

Each vector turns by position × θ. Their absolute turns differ, but the angle between them is determined by the gap.

2 → 8absolute positions j → i
6relative distance i − j
60°relative rotation (i − j)θ
0.500normalized dot-product score
R(iθ)q · R(jθ)k = q · R((j − i)θ)k Only the difference i − j survives.
What to try: change the distance and the score changes. Then move both tokens together: their absolute positions change, but the distance, relative angle and score stay fixed. That is the central RoPE property.
Scope of this visual: it isolates one 2D pair and uses θ = 10° per token. Real RoPE repeats the same operation across many dimension pairs at different rotation rates. A computable rotation at a new position does not, by itself, guarantee that a model will work well beyond its training length.
